title: Alignment microplan: Product + Eng + Applied ML roadmap prep
content:
Context and intent:
- Quick personal prep doc for the cross-functional alignment sync (Product / Eng / Applied ML). Goal: leave with a small, actionable microplan for Q2 deliverables that reduces ambiguity between roadmap lanes: hosted API, Dedicated, and Private.
- Keep conversation focused on 3 things: (1) priority lanes + one measurable success metric each, (2) gating criteria for canary/rollout, (3) immediate blocking experiments from Applied ML that change perf/cost tradeoffs.

Participants to call out in meeting (highly tentative):
- Priya (PM, Hosted API) — customer impact & SLAs
- Marcus (Eng, Serving runtime) — perf/latency risk surface + infra effort estimates
- Elena (Applied ML) — quantization/kv-cache experiments roadmap and expected deltas
- Riley (owner of this note) — synthesize and own follow-ups

Top-level agenda (40 minutes):
1) 5m Quick status: what changed since last alignment (data points)
   - New perf bench: PV1 20% tail latency regression on 8k context with q3 kernels (Marcus)
   - Early canary on Dedicated showed 8% token-cost reduction with sticky-prefix cache (Elena)
2) 15m Priority lanes & success metrics (Product-led framing)
   - Hosted API: reduce 95th tail latency for small-chat workloads to <150ms (measure: 95p from prod traces)
   - Dedicated: improve predictable throughput by +30% for 4x commited pools (measure: sustained tokens/s)
   - Private: cert readiness for KMS + audit logging for 1 regulated customer (measure: audit pass checklist)
   - Quick ask: which of these do we treat as "must hit" vs "nice to have" for the next 8 weeks?
3) 10m Gating criteria for model rollouts/canaries
   - Safety net: if eval suite quality delta > 1.5% on core prompts, block rollout
   - Perf gate: any regression >5% on production 95p latency blocks canary expansion
   - Cost gate: per-token cost >3% increase without commensurate quality improvement => hold
   - Ask Product: acceptable tradeoff ranges for hosted vs dedicated customers
4) 10m Applied ML experiments that materially change prioritization
   - Elena: quantized 4-bit profile on small-chat reduces memory by 2x; unknown tail latency impact for long-context
   - KV caching prototype: sticky-prefix vs per-request caching tradeoffs; early results show cache hit rate depends heavily on prompt templating
   - Discussion: what experiments need infra support vs can be run in researcher sandbox

Key questions I want answered in the sync (so I can write the microplan):
- From Product: which lane unlocks highest customer-facing value in next 8 weeks? (pick 1)
- From Eng: what is realistic parallel capacity for two concurrent canaries vs sequenced?
- From Applied ML: which experiment has the biggest chance to shift priority (quality or cost delta)?

Risks to call out proactively:
- Performance surprises: optimized kernels sometimes regress on longer contexts — need a synthetic/trace-based test that mirrors prod sequences (Marcus action)
- Eval coverage: our core prompt set is biased to short-chat; applied-ml needs to add long-context prompts to avoid blindspots (Elena action)
- Cross-team dependencies: infra provisioning lead time for Dedicated can push planned canaries by 2–3 sprints

Proposed microplan (post-meeting outcome I will draft live):
- Week 0–2: Freeze definitions + metrics + gating rules
  - Deliverable: one-pager that lists lane, owner, success metric, and 2 gating rules
- Week 2–5: Run prioritized experiments
  - Applied ML runs quantization + cache experiments (Elena)
  - Eng provides a perf-heavy test harness and trace replay (Marcus)
- Week 5–8: Evaluate canary and decide rollout path
  - If perf & quality gates pass: proceed to progressive rollout
  - If any gate fails: implement rollback + mitigation plan, and schedule follow-up 2-week fix iteration

Initial follow-up action items (I will own the tracker unless stated):
- Riley: Draft microplan one-pager and share w/ attendees by EOD next Monday (2026-04-05).
- Marcus: Build a short trace-replay harness for 95p latency analysis and post initial results by 2026-04-09.
- Elena: Expand eval prompt set with 100 long-context prompts and run quantization profile by 2026-04-07. Include per-prompt quality delta table.
- Priya: Confirm customer cohorts for Hosted vs Dedicated prioritization and surface top 3 customers who will be impacted by latency/cost tradeoffs by 2026-04-06.
- All: Add any blocking infra tickets to the shared board (JIRA-RI-5123 is placeholder) before the end of week.

Notes to self for meeting facilitation (short):
- Start by asking Product to pick the one priority lane — frame as "what do we want to be able to tell execs in 8 weeks?"
- Keep timer on gating rules discussion — if it stalls, move to experiments and collect asynchronous answers on tradeoffs
- Capture decisions live in the one-pager template (title: lane | owner | metric | gates | next actions)

Loose brainstormed ideas (not for meeting unless asked):
- Lightweight rollout shadowing: mirror live traffic to Dedicated canary without returning responses to customers; measure delta cost/latency nonintrusively
- "Quality delta budget": allow a tiny drop in some prompts if it reduces cost by X, but only if no degradation on critical prompts (treat as weighted metric)
- Run small auto-A/B where 5% traffic uses quantized variant with internal telemetry to catch subtle hallucination regressions

Open questions I will try to resolve pre-meeting:
- Does SRE have capacity to support 2 hardware-provisioning requests in parallel? (check with Raj)
- Is there an existing perf test suite that replays customer sessions end-to-end (not just token-level benches)? (ask Marcus)
- What's the current rolling-window 95p latency for hosted small-chat (need to cite number in meeting)? (ask telemetry)

Quick links / references for attendees:
- JIRA-RI-5123 (infra provisioning tracker)
- CONFLUENCE-PLAT-234 (rollout guardrail draft)
- github.com/redwood-inference/bench/traces (trace repo, private)

Bottom line I want after the sync:
- A 1-page microplan with: chosen priority lane, owner, metric, two gating rules, and 4 concrete follow-ups with owners + dates.

Extra: small template I will paste into the meeting doc for live capture:
- Lane: [Hosted / Dedicated / Private]
- Owner: [name]
- Metric: [primary success metric + measurement method]
- Gating rules: [quality gate; perf gate; cost gate]
- Next actions (owner, date)

End of scratchpad.

(If meeting runs long: ask attendees to drop notes in this doc directly — I will collate.)
